conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion: Supported.** High-quality randomized-trial and regulatory-label evidence indicates that daily subcutaneous abaloparatide reduces *new vertebral fractures* in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis over 18 months.

In the phase 3 ACTIVE randomized clinical trial, abaloparatide reduced new morphometric vertebral fractures by **86% relative to placebo** (p<0.001). The FDA label reports vertebral-fracture incidences at 18 months of **0.6% with abaloparatide versus 4.2% with placebo** (p<0.0001), an absolute reduction of about 3.6 percentage points. These findings apply specifically to the studied postmenopausal osteoporosis population and treatment duration; they do not establish the same magnitude of benefit for every patient or duration.

This evidence aligns with the Endocrine Society recommendation of teriparatide or abaloparatide (up to two years) for postmenopausal women at very high fracture risk to reduce vertebral and nonvertebral fractures.

Sources:  
- https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2544640  
- https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/208743lbl.pdf  
- https://www.endocrine.org/clinical-practice-guidelines/osteoporosis-in-postmenopausal-women
